_comment: Example Claude-Code settings.json hooks fragment. JSON has no comments, so notes live in _comment keys (Claude Code ignores unknown keys). Merge the hooks block into your own settings.json.
_comment_behavior_layer: The behavior layer is NOT delivered by a hook, and this is deliberate. Load it from your instructions file instead: copy `behavior-layer.example.md` into your project as `behavior-layer.md` and add a single line `@behavior-layer.md` to your CLAUDE.md (or paste the layer inline if your tool has no import syntax). WHY NOT A HOOK: a SessionStart hook that prints the file (`cat behavior-layer.md`) looks like it works, but hook stdout is capped — we measured truncation at roughly 2 KB — and the cut is SILENT, mid-file, with no warning. A behavior layer is a few KB by nature, so the hook route delivers a fraction of it and quietly drops the rest of your reflexes. An instructions-file import is loaded verbatim, with no cap. Do not re-add a SessionStart hook here for this purpose.

hooks._comment_PreToolUse: A PreToolUse command hook can validate a tool argument against an allowlist and BLOCK the call (exit non-zero) before it runs — e.g. guarding a tag / label set so only an approved vocabulary is ever written. Point its command at your own validator script. Shown here as a commented pattern, not active. Hooks are the right tool for GATING a call; they are the wrong tool for injecting a large block of text.
